thread:
sam: Heads up — gpu-operator v1.8.0 was rolled to us-west yesterday via helm canary. After the rollout we started seeing GPU workloads stuck Pending with 'no compatible devices' on ~30% of nodes. Anyone else?

jia: yup seeing it. device-plugin pods on affected nodes crashloop and emit: `failed to validate driver/cuda: kernel module not found`

michael: saw similar errors in node-exporter logs: `nvidia: module 525 not loaded, found 470` — looks like operator bumped validations to require driver >=525. We have a mixed fleet (some nodes on older AMI/kernel).

anya: quick repro from a failing node:
```
$ kubectl describe pod gpu-train-xyz
Events:\n  Type    Reason     Age   From               Message
  ----    ------     ----  ----               -------
  Warning FailedScheduling  2m    default-scheduler  0/20 nodes are available: 12 node(s) had no available device plugin, 8 node(s) had insufficient nvidia.com/gpu.
```

jia: device-plugin logs (snippet):
```
E0412 09:12:01.123 deviceplugin.go:235] validation failed: kernel mismatch: expected module v525, found v470; refusing to advertise resources
```

opsbot: Deploy job #deploy-gpu-20270411 (gpu-operator v1.8.0) finished at 2027-04-11T03:22:10Z :white_check_mark:

sam: Important: this isn't a kubelet/CRI failure — device plugin is intentionally rejecting nodes because of driver/CUDA alignment checks introduced in v1.8.0. That's why pods are Pending rather than 'ImagePullBackOff' or similar.

sre-lead: Scope: only us-west region? or across regions?

michael: Mostly us-west-2a and 2b where we still have older AMIs (scheduled for next-month replacement). us-east and europe are on AMI-20270401 with driver 525+ so they're fine.

anya: NCCL errors also reported by some jobs that did schedule elsewhere: `NCCL error "unsupported operation"` — probably from mixed CUDA runtime versions when cross-node comms start.

jia: quick mitigation options I can think of:
- rollback gpu-operator to v1.7.2 (removes strict validation)
- patch node pool drivers (upgrade nvidia driver + reboot) — longer, needs maintenance window
- modify device-plugin config to temporarily disable strict driver check (if operator allows)

sam: I already started a canary rollback on the smallest affected pool to validate. Rolling back operator immediately fixes device-plugin behavior in the canary nodes (ads resources reappear).

michael: Can we autoscale around this? If scheduler sees fewer nodes with advertised GPUs, it will try to place on other pools and we risk overloading dedicated capacity and hitting budget caps. We might burn through burst credits if we start spinning up on-demand clusters. Cost risk is real.

sre-lead: Please pause any automated cluster autoscaling for GPU pools until we have the plan — add quota guardrails.

opsbot: Autoscaler paused on gpu-dedicated-pool-west by @sre-lead at 2027-04-12T09:30:05Z

jia: Logs from the operator reconcile loop show it's also attempting to inject a newer device-plugin daemonset template. If we rollback, we need to ensure it doesn't re-apply on subsequent operator reconcilations. Doing helm rollback + pinning chart version should work.

anya: For longer-term: we need a coordinated upgrade playbook — driver/AMI, kernel, and operator changes must go together. Also consider adding an operator feature-flag to allow soft-fail for mismatched drivers (advertise but mark degraded) so scheduling can continue and we catch incompatible nodes at pod runtime rather than during advertising.

sam: Current status (09:57 UTC):
- Canary rollback completed: canary nodes advertise GPUs again
- Rollback to be applied to remaining pools after approval from infra-schedule (target window 02:00-06:00 UTC)
- Created infra ticket #INFRA-2147 to schedule node AMI/driver upgrades and re-run operator bump as coordinated change

michael: Also flagging cost team: potential short-term spike if we failover workloads to on-demand pools. cc @finance (we'll attach estimate in the ticket).

jia: FYI snippets for debugging if anyone faces it later:
```
# check device-plugin state
kubectl -n kube-system get ds nvidia-device-plugin -o wide
# view plugin logs on node
kubectl -n kube-system logs ds/nvidia-device-plugin -l kubernetes.io/hostname=ip-10-0-1-23
# check kernel module
ssh node && sudo modinfo nvidia | head -n 3
```

sre-lead: Good runbook. After rollback we'll schedule a controlled re-upgrade with node drains in batches, validate kernel module load across pools, and then reapply operator v1.8.0 with a canary gating on driver version.

sam: Thanks everyone — keeping thread pinned to INFRA-2147. Will update here when the full rollout schedule is set. :thumbsup:
